Rachel / Connor —

Thanks for flagging. Below are two drafting paths we can use; both preserve the overall liability cap but limit Redwood's exposure to reasonable, demonstrable costs. I prefer option B for clarity and market alignment, but option A is the seller-friendlier fallback.

Option A (narrow defined carve-out):
"Notwithstanding Section 10 (Limitation of Liability), the cap shall not apply to amounts payable by Redwood that are solely and directly the reasonable documented costs incurred to: (a) restore, recover or reconstitute Customer Data lost or corrupted as a direct result of Redwood's grossly negligent acts or willful misconduct; or (b) remediate verified security breaches caused by Redwood's breach of its obligations under the Security Addendum. Such costs shall not include amounts for lost profits, lost business opportunity, or loss of reputation or goodwill. The aggregate liability for such data restoration costs shall not exceed the greater of (i) the fees paid by Customer under the Order Form for the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to liability, and (ii) $250,000."

Option B (structured carve-out with example buckets):
"Notwithstanding Section 10, amounts resulting from remediation and restoration activities shall be treated as direct damages to the extent they meet all of the following: (i) are reasonably incurred; (ii) are the proximate and direct result of Redwood's material breach that caused unrecoverable loss or corruption of Customer Data; and (iii) are limited to documented third-party costs (for example: data re-ingestion fees, third-party forensics and recovery services, and temporary compute/storage costs). Direct damages under this paragraph expressly exclude lost profits, loss of business, loss of goodwill, and other consequential or punitive categories. The aggregate liability for remediation and restoration costs shall be capped at the total fees paid by Customer under the Order Form in the twelve (12) months prior to the event."

Negotiation guidance:
- If Nimbus insists on 1x ARR and their ARR >> 12 months of Order Form fees, propose a compromise: use the 12-month fees standard but permit a one-time uplift to 1.25x with a materiality threshold (e.g., only if demonstrable third-party recovery costs exceed $500k).
- Keep lost profits/lost goodwill expressly excluded — market expects this.
- Avoid open-ended wording like "all reasonable costs" without the proximate cause / third-party limitation.

I'll draft redlines for Option B (preferable) and include fallback A. Rachel — if you want, I can draft a short negotiation script for you to send to procurement.

Laura

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for the redlines and for surfacing the ask. Our legal team reviewed and proposed language that tries to strike the balance you described — we preserve the excluded categories (lost profits, goodwill) but allow a narrow, documented cost carve-out for data recovery. See the proposed insertion below (we'd like to put this in Section 10.3):

"For the avoidance of doubt, and notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, amounts consisting solely of documented third-party costs reasonably incurred to restore or re-ingest Customer Data that is irretrievably lost or corrupted as a direct result of Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct shall be treated as direct damages and not subject to the monetary cap in Section 10.1, provided that such amounts do not include lost profits, loss of business opportunity, loss of goodwill, or any other indirect, special or consequential damages. The aggregate liability for such documented restoration costs shall be limited to the greater of (a) the fees paid by Customer under the Order Form for the twelve (12) months preceding the event, and (b) $250,000."

If Nimbus wants the 1x ARR figure, Laura suggested we offer a compromise: keep the 12-month fees cap but allow a single exception to 1.25x with a high materiality threshold (third-party invoices > $500k). Happy to discuss.

Next steps: if that language is acceptable we can incorporate it into your redline and move to DocuSign. Connor — can you confirm that procurement will accept the compromise on timing / PO flow?

Best,
Rachel
